prompt: What does super.methodName() do inside a subclass method?
choices: Calls the method on a newly created parent object
Calls the parent class's version of that method
Makes the method private in the subclass
Prevents the method from being overridden further
explanation: super.methodName() explicitly invokes the parent's implementation. Useful when overriding: you can call super.draw() to run the parent drawing logic and then add subclass-specific drawing on top.
